<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via AutomationResult (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/api/declarative-endpoints.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/:name/trigger (route, bridged from symbol TriggerFlowResponseSchema — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via AutomationResult (symbol, a top-level interface), /api/v1/automation/:name/trigger (route, bridged from symbol TriggerFlowResponseSchema — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/:name/trigger (route, bridged from symbol TriggerFlowResponseSchema — its route source's handler names it))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via AutomationResult (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via AutomationResult (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationResult (symbol, a top-level interface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **172** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e40cd1e28dd79e60e7f4be0db06f071f3f962574` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2c3940812e33a8fbac9050eae85d3348446cab9a` — the merge of head `4da1fb68df06244e029b1644db5846664572116c` into base `e40cd1e28dd79e60e7f4be0db06f071f3f962574`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2c3940812e33a8fbac9050eae85d3348446cab9a && git checkout 2c3940812e33a8fbac9050eae85d3348446cab9a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e40cd1e28dd79e60e7f4be0db06f071f3f962574 4da1fb68df06244e029b1644db5846664572116c && git checkout -B drift-repro e40cd1e28dd79e60e7f4be0db06f071f3f962574 && git merge --no-ff 4da1fb68df06244e029b1644db5846664572116c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e40cd1e28dd79e60e7f4be0db06f071f3f962574
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e40cd1e28dd79e60e7f4be0db06f071f3f962574` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4da1fb68df06244e029b1644db5846664572116c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + none

Inputs read: card #33402 (body and its three comments: triage 6884924903, claim 6885523313, os-dev-report 6885846785; no earlier review record), PR #33519 (body, 4 files, net diff against `main`, one commit on merge-base `f068cde8`), and the check-runs on this head. The producers were read at the head with `git show`; `main` has not moved any of them, nor the two `hits` files, since the merge-base.

Check-runs on the head as read (50): 14 `success`, 13 `skipped`, 23 `in_progress`, 0 failed. Completed green: Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Flag docs affected by code changes, Dogfood Regression Gate, Plan Test UI shards, Auto Label, filter. Still running: Check Changeset (read `success` on the first read of the check-runs, `in_progress` on the second, a newer run), Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), Lint (ESLint, repo & tooling gates, docs & code guards, CI release & engine gates, scoped slot lookup & corpus, scoped query-options erasure), Live E2E UI. The generated-reference drift gate (`check:generated` / `check:docs`) sits in the running lint families, so it is NOT yet answered by CI on this head. This verdict is the design judgment; the merge still waits on those runs.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: unchanged. RIGHT. Every hunk in the two `hits` files is JSDoc or a `.describe()` string. No `z.` call, key, enum member, `.optional()`, export or type is touched; the same input parses to the same output on both sides of the diff.
- Public surface: three description strings move, nothing else. RIGHT. `TriggerFlowResponseSchema` result `innerRefusal` describe, `FlowFailureDetailsSchema.innerRefusal` describe, and the JSDoc of `FlowInnerRefusalSchema`, `FlowFailureDetailsSchema` and `AutomationResult.innerRefusal`. The describe text ships in spec `dist` and the JSDoc in its declarations.
- Generated reference: `content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx` moves exactly the two `innerRefusal` rows (`FlowFailureDetails`, `AutomationResult`), and each row's new text is byte for byte the concatenated describe string of its source. RIGHT. No other generated file is in the diff, and `git grep -i "write met"` at the head finds no remaining sentence about `innerRefusal` in `packages/spec`, `content/docs` or `skills`.
- No behaviour change, so no test and no ablation are owed. RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/33402-inner-refusal-describe.md` is `'@objectstack/spec': patch`. That matches what the diff publishes: description text only, in one package. No other package's published output changes (the `.mdx` is docs, not a package).

Clause-②: no. Present on the PR body and in the changeset, with `Metadata-protocol: none` on both. Correct: nothing a consumer could parse, author or call yesterday is refused, renamed or re-typed today.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, surface: the card listed only `automation-api.zod.ts`; the claim (6885523313) added `contracts/automation-service.ts:771` to the file surface before the work started. The diff stays inside the claimed surface (two sources, the generated reference, one changeset). Answered.
- Dev flag, the one clause beyond "write met": "the data layer gave the node" became "the data layer (or the function resolver) gave the node". Accepted: without it the sentence is false for the `script` producer (see ④).
- `out_of_scope_findings` (two, both `carrier: none`): the comments at `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts:416-420` and `inner-refusal.ts:54-64` still describe the member as the data nodes' alone. Confirmed by reading both at the head. They are comments outside this card's surface and outside the diff, so not reviewed here and no bar to this PR. ESCALATED to the seat: they have no carrier, so the seat files one p3 card for them or records them as accepted. This record does not file it.

### ④ Design judgment

The new sentence, in all five sites: "the refusal a node met inside the run (a data node's read or write, or a `script` node's function resolution)".

Producers, read at the head. `innerRefusal` is minted in one place only, `refusalCarriedBy` (`inner-refusal.ts:86`), and it has five call sites:

| Call site | What threw | Fits the sentence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `builtin/crud-nodes.ts:669` `get_record` catch | `data.find` / `data.findOne` | a data node's read |
| `builtin/crud-nodes.ts:831` `create_record` catch | the insert | a data node's write |
| `builtin/crud-nodes.ts:947` `update_record` catch | the update | a data node's write |
| `builtin/crud-nodes.ts:1026` `delete_record` catch | the delete | a data node's write |
| `builtin/screen-nodes.ts:659` `script` | `engine.resolveFunction` throwing `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` (`status` 409, `code` `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`) | a `script` node's function resolution |

Every other path that puts the member on a result only CARRIES one of those five: `dag-traversal.ts:519` brands the node failure and `:1595`, `engine.ts:8097` and `run-resume.ts:2264` read the brand at the terminal exits; `subflow-node.ts:178`, `map-node.ts:288` and `run-resume.ts:1550` copy a child run's; `try-catch-node.ts:244/356` and `engine.ts:11194` carry the last attempt's or the catch region's. In each, the refusal was still met by a data node or a `script` node inside the run (or its child run), so the sentence holds. The runtime doors (`flow-dispatch-status.ts:268`) and the MCP reader (`mcp-http-tools.ts:805`) pass it on verbatim.

- No producer is left out. The four `crud-nodes.ts` executors are the only `category: 'data'` executors; `connector_action`, `http`, `notify`, `wait`, `screen`, `decision`, `assignment`, `loop`, `parallel` and `save_notice` never set the member.
- Nothing is over-claimed. The `script` clause says "function resolution", not the function's own run: the handler's catch (`screen-nodes.ts:706-713`) sets no member, and the unchanged "Absent on every other failure (a script that threw, …)" in the same JSDoc still says so. `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` is a standard-catalog member (`api/errors.zod.ts:95`) that `ErrorCode` (`api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts:1968`) includes, so the produced value parses against `FlowInnerRefusalSchema`; `flow-function-package-scope.test.ts:134` pins it.
- "(or the function resolver)" is correct: the `script` refusal comes from the package-scoped resolver, not the data layer.
- First consumers (the flow doors' `FLOW_FAILED` details, the MCP tool's message ladder) read `code` and `message` and never the description, so no consumer changes.
- Attempt to break it: two failures a reader might expect under the new wording do not fill the member. An unregistered function name (`screen-nodes.ts:662-668`, the resolver's `not-found`, not a refusal) and `get_record`'s pre-engine `storedMetadataFilterRefusal` return. Both are consistent with the text, which every site still closes with "only when a refusal was met" / "Absent when the failure met no refusal": the sentence states which nodes can fill it, not that every failure of theirs does. No finding.

Findings:

- **N1 (nit).** `FlowInnerRefusalSchema.code`'s describe ("the ADR-0112 member a record save of the same write answers in `error.code`"), the same phrase in that schema's Semantics JSDoc, and "the shape a record save of the same write answers with" in the contract JSDoc keep a write-only comparison. For a read refusal or a resolver refusal there is no "same write". It names the code's spelling, not which node fills the member, and the sentence above it now says the latter, so it has no effect on correctness or the contract. The PR body names it as left on purpose. A fix would be in a `hits` file and would move the head: leave it as an accepted deviation, or carry it on a follow-up card.
- **N2 (nit).** The unchanged "The problem it solves" paragraph still says "met by a flow's write node". It is history of the defect that B′ closed, accurate as history. No change asked.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-qecamw`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5mecqk8M5q9vjKj6aS`

**VERDICT: PASS**
